answer.rationale: PR#1243 is described as 'a collection of small, independent fixes for test and doctest failures' with 'No functional changes to the library API'. It patches CI/doctest robustness (shape->reshape, complex-to-real casts, dropped warning check, platform-dependent numerics in tests) rather than correcting any floating-point computation in the library. No numerical defect is fixed.
answer.evidence: [pr_body:PR#1243] 'A collection of small, independent fixes for test and doctest failures appearing in CI. No functional changes to the library API.'; bandwidth() doctests switched to '+ELLIPSIS' because 'the last digit or two of the repr varies across SciPy/BLAS builds' — a test-platform accommodation, not a library numerics fix.

answer.rationale: The matched c2d/sample method returned an all-NaN numerator for systems with a pole or zero at s=0, because the DC-gain match divides dcgain (inf or 0) by zgain (0 or inf), yielding 0/0 or inf/inf. The defect is a mishandled/inf/NaN-producing singularity rather than precision loss or an iterative divergence; the fix reformulates the gain so the vanishing origin factor no longer generates a special value.
answer.evidence: commit: 'returned an all-NaN numerator for any system with a pole or zero at s = 0'; PR#1241: 'zgain becomes 0 or inf while dcgain is simultaneously inf or 0, giving 0/0 or inf/inf'; diff comment: '0/0 or inf/inf -> a NaN numerator'.

answer.triggering_input: A SISO continuous TransferFunction with a pole or zero at s = 0, e.g. ct.tf([1.], [1., 0.]) or ct.tf([2., 5.], [1., 0.]), sampled with method='matched'.
answer.triggering_condition: Calling ct.sample_system / TransferFunction.sample with method='matched' on an origin pole/zero system. The DC-gain match divides by the vanishing 1 - z factor of the origin pole/zero, so zgain is 0 or inf while dcgain is inf or 0, giving 0/0 or inf/inf.
answer.buggy_behavior: The matched conversion returns an all-NaN numerator: e.g. integrator 1/s gives num = [nan] and den = [1. -1.]; PI controller gives num = [nan nan] and den = [1. -1.]. The gain match is undefined at the origin singularity.
answer.expected_behavior: After the fix, the origin factors are left out of the gain product and their scaling is restored via the z - 1 ~ s*T limit. The result has finite numerator and denominator, recovers textbook matched transforms (1/s^k -> T^k/(z-1)^k), and matches |G(jw)| near the origin.

input_output_examples.expected_output: np.all(np.isfinite(sys_dt.num[0][0])) and np.all(np.isfinite(sys_dt.den[0][0])); |G_d(e^jwT)| -> |G_c(jw)| at w=1e-3/dt, rtol=1e-4

input_output_examples.buggy_output: all-NaN numerator (origin pole at s=0; buggy revision)

input_output_examples.input: ct.sample_system(ct.tf([1., 0.], [1., 2., 5.]), 0.1, method='matched')  # differentiator, zero at s=0
input_output_examples.buggy_output: all-NaN numerator from the vanishing origin zero factor (buggy revision)
input_output_examples.expected_output: np.all(np.isfinite(sys_dt.num[0][0])) and np.all(np.isfinite(sys_dt.den[0][0])); gain matched at w=1e-3/dt

answer.expected_failing_behavior: matched c2d of systems with a pole/zero at s=0 (integrator, PI, type-1/2) gives an all-NaN numerator from 0/0 DC-gain matching; tests assert finite num/den, textbook Ts**k/(z-1)**k coefficients, and low-frequency gain match.

answer.compiler: setuptools.build_meta (build backend); no compiler is specified for control. README notes C/Fortran compilers and Python development files are needed only if pip-installing Slycot.
answer.runtime_version: Python; CI uses 3.12 (conda-forge). pyproject requires-python >=3.10 and classifiers 3.10, 3.11, 3.12.
system_packages: Miniconda/Conda with conda-forge and defaults channels
conda packages: python=3.12, numpy, matplotlib, scipy, slycot, pmw, jupyter, ipython!=9.0, cvxopt, pandas
build_commands: conda create --name control-examples-env --channel conda-forge --strict-channel-priority --quiet --yes python=3.12 pip numpy matplotlib scipy slycot pmw jupyter ipython!=9.0
answer.conflicts: README says install from source via pip install .; CI instead creates a conda-forge env (python=3.12) then pip install . in it. README/docs say pytest -v or pytest --pyargs control -v, but CI runs examples/notebooks scripts and doctest + PYTHONPATH=../ pytest. pyproject requires-python >=3.10 while CI uses 3.12.

answer.rationale: The PR fixes a linear-algebra semantics bug (MIMO LTI scalar multiplication was scaling by a constant matrix instead of a scaled identity) and an FRD construction exception: with fewer than 4 frequency points the default degree-3 spline fit was requested and SciPy requires k+1 points, so it raised ValueError. Both are API/logic faults: the first is wrong array/scalar semantics, the second is a bad default parameter producing an exception, not a wrong floating-point value, NaN/Inf, divergence, or instability around a conditional test.
answer.evidence: [pr_body] 'multiplying a MIMO LTI system by a constant was multiplying by a matrix filled with the constant rather than a diagonal matrix'; 'default degree of the fit was 3. The SciPy interpolation function requires k+1 data points ... so an exception was generated.'; [diff:control/frdata.py:261-280] 'degree = 3 if self.omega.size > 3 else self.omega.size - 1' / 'k=degree'.
